Conditional Class Probabilities of a Two-Latent-Variable Model

Source: R/derived_estimates.R
joint_probabilities.Rd

P(y = j | x = k) at given covariate values, from a fit_joint_classes() fit, with delta-method standard errors and intervals (derived_estimates()). The fit's own conditional table averages over the sample's covariates; this one fixes them, which is how a moderated association is described: the probabilities among men and among women, say.

Usage

joint_probabilities(fit, at = NULL, level = 0.95)

Arguments

fit

A fit_joint_classes() fit.

at

A named list or vector of covariate values for the covariates on y. Covariates not named are held at 0. NULL (the default) holds all at 0.

level

Confidence level of the intervals.

Value

A data frame with columns x, y, estimate, se, lower, upper, one row per pair of classes.

Examples

# \donttest{
set.seed(1)
n  <- 800
w  <- rbinom(n, 1, 0.5)
cx <- sample(1:2, n, TRUE)
cy <- ifelse(runif(n) < plogis(-1 + 2 * (cx == 1) + w * (cx == 1)), 1L, 2L)
A  <- sapply(1:4, function(j) rbinom(n, 1, ifelse(cx == 1, 0.85, 0.15)))
S  <- sapply(1:4, function(j) rbinom(n, 1, ifelse(cy == 1, 0.85, 0.15)))
fit <- fit_joint_classes(A, S, predictors_y = data.frame(w = w),
                         y_effects = "by_x", n_init = 5, random_state = 1)
joint_probabilities(fit, at = list(w = 1))
#>     x   y  estimate         se     lower     upper
#> 1 X#1 Y#1 0.6976749 0.03939720 0.6204578 0.7748920
#> 2 X#1 Y#2 0.3023251 0.03939720 0.2251080 0.3795422
#> 3 X#2 Y#1 0.1103566 0.02845141 0.0545929 0.1661204
#> 4 X#2 Y#2 0.8896434 0.02845141 0.8338796 0.9454071
# }
